subject: Deployment readiness matrix & acceptance criteria — PioneerApps private GPU pool
messages:

Cc: procurement@pioneerapps.com
Date: Fri, 27 Nov 2026 09:05:00 -0800
Subject: Deployment readiness matrix & acceptance criteria — PioneerApps private GPU pool

Alex / team — thanks again for the sync this week. PioneerApps' procurement and infra teams want a short, actionable checklist we can use to validate the private VPC deployment before cutover.

Goal: ship the first production-capacity private GPU pool for PioneerApps in their us-west VPC and have clear, measurable acceptance criteria for throughput, latency, and failover behavior.

What I need from ENG ops (Ben/Hannah):
- A concise readiness matrix (single sheet) with pass/fail criteria we can use in procurement.
- Target throughput and latency numbers for the initial model (LlamaX-13B quantized) and the scaling policy we recommend.
- Network egress requirements and any special routing or firewall rules Pioneer needs to pre-provision.

I attached a draft matrix and the latest network diagram. Alex — if you can provide one sample traffic csv and confirm the SLA floor Pioneer needs for p95 latency, we will bake it into the matrix.

Timeline: Pioneer wants a validation window next week (week of Dec 6). Can we have the readiness matrix and runbook by EOD next Wednesday (Dec 2)?

Thanks — I’ll coordinate procurement expectations once we have the pass/fail items.

—Sean

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Alex Rivera <alex@pioneerapps.com>
Date: Fri, 27 Nov 2026 10:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Deployment readiness matrix & acceptance criteria — PioneerApps private GPU pool

Sean / Alex — high level reply with the numbers we'll use in the matrix. I'll attach a short checklist and a capacity sketch.

Summary targets (baseline):
- Model: LlamaX-13B (INT8 / 4-bit sim) serving 128-token generative prompts.
- Sustained throughput target (initial): 120 req/s (short median prompt), burst up to 200 req/s for 10m windows.
- Latency SLO: p95 < 220ms end-to-end for 128-token generations; p99 < 450ms.
- Token-rate estimate: ~35k tokens/sec per 8x A10080GB pool node under mixed batching assumptions.
- Baseline pool: 6x A100 nodes (80GB) recommended for initial commit to meet sustained 120 req/s with 20% headroom.

Scaling policy (recommended):
- Autoscale triggers: add 2 nodes when 3 metrics are met for 2 consecutive 60s intervals: GPU memory usage > 70% OR request queue depth > 45 OR average per-GPU token throughput > 80% of observed baseline.
- Scale down: remove 1 node when queue depth < 15 and GPU memory < 50% for 5m. Min pool size = 4 nodes, max pool size = 12 nodes for initial contract.
- Warm pool: keep 10% of capacity warmed (hot KV caches) before anticipated bursts (we recommend pre-warm before marketing campaigns).

Network / infra considerations:
- NIC: 100Gbps capable infra recommended; practical egress per node observed ~8–10 Gbps under heavy token output. Reserve 8 Gbps per node for worst-case.
- Latency: keep cross-AZ traffic to a minimum; recommend single-AZ deployment in PioneerApps us-west VPC for initial cutover.
- NAT/Egress: allocate static NAT IPs and allow TLS port 443 outbound to Redwood control plane for health checks and KV sync.

Acceptance tests (what will pass):
1) Sustained run for 60 minutes at 120 req/s with p95 < 220ms and no queue saturation.
2) 10-minute burst test at 200 req/s with graceful degradation (no more than 2x p95) and autoscale adding nodes within 90s.
3) Node failover: simulate N+1 fail and validate traffic reroutes within 60s and no more than 10% increased latency.

I'll drop the readiness matrix workbook and a one-page runbook in the thread. Hannah — can you add the exact steps for KV warm/cool operations (cache TTLs + recommended pre-warm API calls)?

Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Platform Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

Attachments referenced: pioneer_traffic_sample.csv (placeholder), readiness_checklist.md

From: Alex Rivera <alex@pioneerapps.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@pioneerapps.com
Date: Fri, 27 Nov 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Deployment readiness matrix & acceptance criteria — PioneerApps private GPU pool

Thanks Sean/Ben — the numbers look reasonable. A few clarifications from our side before procurement signs off: 

1) p95 target: PioneerApps requires p95 < 250ms for the initial SLA (we can accept 220ms as a stretch target).
2) Bursts: our marketing-driven bursts historically last ~15 minutes and can reach 250 req/s peak for very short windows. We need to ensure the autoscale behavior can handle that or we have a documented throttling strategy.
3) Egress/firewall: we will only provision static NATs on our side — is that sufficient for control-plane callbacks and health checks?

Attached is a 24-hour sample traffic CSV (column: timestamp, requests/sec) — it has two spike windows that represent real-world behavior.

Next steps: please update the readiness matrix to reflect the p95 acceptance item and add a short throttling fallback we can use if autoscale lags (e.g., graceful rejection with 429 and Retry-After). Procurement asks that we include a simple pass/fail checklist they can sign off on.

—Alex Rivera
Head of Platform, PioneerApps
alex@pioneerapps.com

Perfect — thanks for the quick turnaround, Ben. Alex, noted on p95 < 250ms and the larger 15-minute bursts up to 250 req/s. We'll update the matrix with those acceptance thresholds and add a short throttling fallback that returns 429 + Retry-After when queue depth exceeds the hard cap and autoscale hasn't completed.

Action items and owners (to hit the Dec 2 deliverable):
- Ben: finalize readiness_matrix_v2.xlsx with the updated acceptance criteria and autoscale tuning (due Tue Nov 30 EOD).
- Hannah: add KV warmup steps + runbook snippet and confirm network egress byte budgeting (due Wed Dec 1 EOD).
- Sean: coordinate with Pioneer procurement on the pass/fail checklist and send procurement-ready doc to procurement@pioneerapps.com (due Wed Dec 2 EOD).

I'll generate a short test plan for the 60-min sustained run and the 15-min burst test; we can book a slot the week of Dec 6 for validation.

If anyone sees a blocker on the timeline, flag it now — otherwise I'll circle back once the v2 matrix is attached.

Thanks — Sean
